message.abstract:
<jats:p><div>
 We develop a graph neural network (GNN) framework for asset pricing with&nbsp;<span>supply chains, nonlinearly aggregating firm-level information across&nbsp;</span><span>$d$-hop neighborhoods. We find that depth $d=3$ empirically balances bias reduction from higher-order relations against variance from added complexity; beyond $d=3$, oversmoothing results in homogeneous embeddings and collapses predictive $R^2$ from $15.3\%$ to&nbsp;</span>
</div>
<div>
 near zero for $d \geq 8$. We leverage rich benchmarks to residualize the supply chain GNN-managed portfolio, which yields an out-of-sample Sharpe ratio of $1.07$.&nbsp;&nbsp;<span>Sensitivity to missing links concentrates in high-centrality rather&nbsp;</span><span>than large-cap firms, consistent with the GNN learning from graph&nbsp;</span><span>topology rather than firm size.</span>
</div></jats:p>
title: Graph Machine Learning for Asset Pricing: Traversing the Supply Chain
